:::{#lem-prediction-error-split}
#### Prediction error splits at the conditional mean

Let $g^*(X) \eqdef \E{Y \mid X}$.
For any prediction function $g(X)$:

$$\prederr_g = \prederr_{g^*} + \paren{g(X) - g^*(X)}$$

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\prederr_g
&= g(X) - Y
&& \text{(definition of } \prederr_g \text{)} \\
&= \paren{g^*(X) - Y} + \paren{g(X) - g^*(X)}
&& \text{(add and subtract } g^*(X) \text{)} \\
&= \prederr_{g^*} + \paren{g(X) - g^*(X)}
&& \text{(definition of } \prederr_{g^*} \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-prediction-error-split}
#### The split in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
when $X = 0$ and $Y = 0$,
the constant prediction $g_1(X) = 3$ has prediction error $\prederr_{g_1} = 3$.
The conditional mean is $g^*(0) = 1$,
so $\prederr_{g^*} = 1$ and $g_1(0) - g^*(0) = 2$,
and $3 = 1 + 2$.

:::
